title: Expose a stable native API for class and property access
description:
Native extensions currently need to depend on S7's internal representation or call back into R to inspect objects. This adds a stable native API for retrieving S7 class definitions and reading properties through their getters.

- `S7_get_class()` returns the stored S7 class definition, resolving shared class references, or `R_NilValue` when there is none.
- `S7_get_prop()` reads a property with the same getter and storage behavior as `prop()`. A non-missing scalar character name is a caller precondition.
- C and C++ packages include `S7-init.h` in their initialization source file, call `S7_init_api()` during DLL initialization, and include `S7.h` elsewhere. Calls use shared function pointers without per-call initialization checks.
- Rust and other bindings can retrieve and cache the registered pointers with `R_GetCCallable()`.

The registered entry points use the existing C implementations directly. Documentation describes the two function contracts and includes a complete example of initialization and property access. A compiled consumer fixture exercises C, C++, direct registered lookup, and repeated header inclusion. The benchmark compares native access with evaluating cached and namespace-qualified R calls.

Local results from [bench/native-api.R](https://github.com/RConsortium/S7/blob/feat/native-api/bench/native-api.R), using R 4.6.1 on an Apple M4 Max with clang `-O2`:

| Operation       | Cached R call via `Rf_eval()` | Native API | Native vs cached R |
| --------------- | ----------------------------: | ---------: | -----------------: |
| Class lookup    |                       0.64 µs |   0.021 µs |         31x faster |
| Stored property |                       0.26 µs |   0.063 µs |        4.1x faster |
| Simple getter   |                        1.2 µs |    0.97 µs |        1.2x faster |

Times are per access: the median of session medians from three fresh R sessions, with 1,000 accesses per C loop. R functions and complete call objects are cached before timing, and all paths repeatedly access the same object. Parsing and call construction are excluded.

Evaluating a namespace-qualified `S7::prop()` call takes 0.32 µs for a stored property versus 0.063 µs through the native API (5.1x faster). Getters still execute R code. Class lookup also avoids the general classification logic in R's `S7_class()`.

Closes #788.

title: Register `@` directly for packaged classes so reads don't scale with class depth
description:
Follow-up to #723 (hot paths found while profiling CVXR, whose S7 class hierarchies go up to eight levels deep).

`x@name` reaches `@.S7_object` through S3 dispatch on `class(x)`, which misses once per inheritance level before it finds the method. This PR registers the same method (`prop()`) under each packaged class's own name, so dispatch hits on the first lookup and the cost of `@` no longer grows with class depth. Behavior is unchanged: it is the same method.

- `new_class()` registers the method and records the class name in the package's `.__S3MethodsTable__.`, which is saved with the package (as S7 already does for external methods).
- `S7_on_load()` re-registers recorded classes, and `S7_on_unload()` removes them.
- Classes without a package are not registered, an existing `@` method is never replaced, and R < 4.3 is untouched.

**Benchmark** (`bench/property-access.R`, 1000 reads per iteration, separate sessions before and after, R 4.6.1, macOS arm64):

| class depth | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 610 µs | 460 µs | 1.3x faster |
| 5 | 790 µs | 460 µs | 1.7x faster |
| 8 | 1.0 ms | 460 µs | 2.2x faster |

`prop()` and `attr()` timings are unchanged. The remaining gap between `@` and `prop()` (~200 µs per 1000 reads) is the fixed cost of base R's S3 dispatch for `@`, which S7 can't avoid.

**Trade-off to weigh:** this adds one entry per packaged S7 class to base R's S3 methods table, managed by the load and unload hooks. If you'd rather not touch that table, the alternative is documenting `prop()` as the fast spelling for hot paths.

**Tests:** new tests in `test-hooks.R` cover registration, no-package classes, not replacing an existing method, load/unload, and an installed package. The full suite passes.

title: Handle str() spacing across R versions
description:
Restore separators in S7's `str()` and `print()` output after R 4.7 changed which call supplies the leading space. Property values retain their separator, and S7 objects nested in lists avoid doubled spaces. Also fix missing spaces before plain lists, data frames, and classed environments, and extra spaces before inherited data such as logical values and empty lists on older R.

Use a shared helper to print property values and inherited data directly, with an R-version flag cached in `.onLoad()`. Extend the existing snapshots for logical values and environment properties, and retain the nested-list fixture while normalizing its base-R spacing difference.

Fixes #791.

Alternative to #792.

Fixes #791.

title: Preserve S4 numeric registration for packages built with older S7
description:
`S4_register()` can fail when numeric properties were stored with S7 0.2.2 and loaded with development S7. The union's member types are unchanged, but its stored constructor and validator functions differ from the current `class_numeric`. This reproduces the error reported in [Data-Wise/medfit#214](https://github.com/Data-Wise/medfit/pull/214#issuecomment-6228577673).

Keep the existing `identical()` check as the fast path. Add a compatibility fallback that recognizes the base integer and double member types and maps them to S4's existing `numeric` class, so these properties can be registered without an extra S4 union. No new functions or arguments are introduced.

Add a public API regression for a numeric union serialized with S7 0.2.2. A `BACKCOMPAT` comment identifies the fallback, regression test, and fixture to remove when support for older package builds is dropped.

title: Preserve method argument expressions on R before 4.4
description:
On R 4.2 and 4.3, deparsing the call recorded by a plain `stop()` inside an S7 method can fail with `'S4SXP': should not happen - please report`. S7 now records the argument expressions, so an error from `g(Foo())` has a readable call such as `` `method(g, Foo)`(x = Foo()) ``. This also applies to warnings and `sys.call()` inside methods.

Internally, builds for R < 4.4 use `applyClosure()` to supply the original argument promises separately from the recorded call. This preserves laziness and `substitute()` behavior, including forwarded `...` and `super()`. The compatibility code uses internal R APIs exposed by those older versions and is excluded from newer builds. R >= 4.4 retains the existing dispatcher. Public regressions cover argument expressions, promise behavior, and the version boundary.

Literal S7 values supplied through `do.call()` still encounter the older base-R deparser limitation; ordinary R functions fail in the same case.

Fixes #783.

title: Use declared S7 ancestry for downcasts
description:
This fixes a conversion failure found in ggplotplus during reverse-dependency checks. `theme_plus()` and `gridlines_plus()` convert `ggplot()` objects to `GGPlotPlusPlot`, an S7 subclass. ggplot2 adds S3 compatibility names such as `"gg"` to its plots, and those extra names caused `convert()` to reject the conversion.

This slightly relaxes the conversion check so those extra S3 names no longer block it. We still check the parent-child relationship using the S7 class definitions. For example, a child with classes `Child → Parent → S7_object` can be constructed from a parent with classes `Parent → S7_object`: the parent's classes match the end of the child's classes exactly, in the same order.

Here is a simplified example:

```r
library(S7)

Parent := new_class(
  properties = list(x = class_double),
  constructor = function(x = 0) {
    object <- new_object(S7_object(), x = x)
    class(object) <- c(class(object), "extra_s3_class")
    object
  }
)
Child := new_class(parent = Parent)

parent <- Parent(x = 1)
class(parent)
# [1] "Parent" "S7_object" "extra_s3_class"

child <- convert(parent, to = Child)
class(child)
# [1] "Child" "Parent" "S7_object"
child@x
# [1] 1
```

Conversion still passes the original object's property values to the subclass constructor. That constructor determines the new object's classes; the extra S3 names are not copied over.

The regressions cover successful conversion with extra S3 names, preservation of property values, and rejection of conversion between sibling classes without an explicit method.

title: Preserve parent constructor arguments for read-only overrides
description:
A generated child constructor can lose an inherited argument when the child makes that property read-only. The parent constructor may still need the argument for initialization or validation.

For example, `Parent` checks that `other_prop` does not exceed `parent_prop`. `Child` makes `parent_prop` read-only by giving it a getter and no setter:

```r
library(S7)

Parent := new_class(
  properties = list(
    parent_prop = new_property(class_numeric, default = 1),
    other_prop = new_property(class_numeric, default = 1)
  ),
  validator = function(self) {
    if (self@other_prop > self@parent_prop) {
      "@other_prop must not exceed @parent_prop"
    }
  }
)

Child := new_class(
  parent = Parent,
  properties = list(
    parent_prop = new_property(class_numeric, getter = \(self) 2)
  )
)
```

Before this fix, `Child(parent_prop = 2, other_prop = 2)` fails with `unused argument (parent_prop = 2)`. With this fix, the generated constructor passes both arguments to `Parent()`, so its validation succeeds. The resulting child still has a read-only property:

```r
child <- Child(parent_prop = 2, other_prop = 2)
child@parent_prop
#> [1] 2

child@parent_prop <- 3
#> Error: Can't set read-only property.
```

The change removes the filtering that dropped these inherited arguments and adds regression coverage. Their defaults are preserved, and the generated constructor does not assign to the child's read-only property.

This came up while investigating dcmstan during reverse-dependency checks. Its `loglinear()`, `hdcm()`, and `bayesnet()` wrappers pass `model` to the parent `structural()` constructor so it can validate `model_args`. This fix lets those subclasses use getter-only `model` properties with generated constructors. dcmstan still needs a separate change to replace its current setters, which error after initialization.

title: Allow property getters to receive the property name
description:
`new_property()` getters can now optionally take `function(self, name)`, so one getter can be reused across properties. This mirrors the existing `function(self, name, value)` setter form. For example, one getter can format two stored text properties:

```r
library(S7)

get_upper <- \(self, name) toupper(prop(self, name))
text_property <- new_property(
  class_character,
  getter = get_upper,
  setter = function(self, name, value) {
    prop(self, name) <- value
    self
  }
)
Label := new_class(
  properties = list(title = text_property, subtitle = text_property)
)

label <- Label(title = "hello", subtitle = "world")
label@title
#> [1] "HELLO"
label@subtitle
#> [1] "WORLD"
```

Inside the getter, `prop(self, name)` reads the stored value without calling the getter again. Existing `function(self)` getters continue to work.

The change updates signature validation and the native getter call, documents both forms, and adds public API tests for shared getters and stored-value access.

title: Preserve inherited constructor arguments when adding computed properties
description:
Adding a read-only computed property to a child class can incorrectly remove an unrelated inherited argument from its generated constructor. In the regression example, `Child` adds `child_prop` and `child_read_only_prop`, but its constructor drops `parent_prop2`.

Constructor generation now matches read-only properties by name. The regression checks that the child accepts both parent arguments and can read its new computed property.

This surfaced during reverse-dependency checks in statim's `class_lm_object()` constructor, which dropped the inherited `family` argument and failed on `family = "gaussian"`.

title: Allow empty vector property defaults without warnings
description:
`new_property()` warns about explicit empty vector defaults even though generated constructors use the same values for implicit base-class defaults. These values can be embedded in a constructor without a code/documentation mismatch.

Accept empty vectors without attributes after checking the property class, and document the accepted defaults. Named or classed empty vectors, nonempty lists, and other complex evaluated defaults still warn and recommend `quote()`.

title: Restore compatibility with saved S7 mappings
description:
Some existing ggforce installations contain saved mappings with an S7 class vector but no stored class metadata. S7 currently rejects these objects, preventing ggforce from loading without a rebuild.

Accept these legacy objects through a small compatibility fallback, with regression coverage for recognition and data access. Keep the fallback clearly marked for removal once affected packages have regenerated their saved mappings. No package dependencies or CI changes are needed.

title: Validate data-frame columns without calling subclass as.list()
description:
Reverse dependency checks found that constructing `fr::fr_tdr` from a valid data frame failed with:

```text
All columns and row names must have the same length
```

The data-frame validator uses `vapply(self, NROW, ...)`. For a classed object, `vapply()` calls `as.list()`. `fr_tdr` defines that method to return metadata, so S7 was checking metadata lengths instead of column lengths.

This change applies `vapply()` to `unclass(self)`, so validation inspects the underlying columns without calling the subclass's conversion method. The columns themselves retain their classes, so matrix and nested data-frame columns still use their row counts. Compact row names keep the existing handling, and the list-type check still rejects environments before `unclass()` runs.

title: Resolve foreign parent classes by exported binding
description:
Reverse dependency checks found that ggplotplus no longer installed with development S7. It defines a class with `parent = ggplot2::class_ggplot`, which failed with:

```text
Package 'ggplot2' must export `ggplot` as an S7 class.
```

The class is named `"ggplot"` internally, but ggplot2 exports it as `class_ggplot`. S7 used the internal name to look up the parent, so it found the `ggplot()` function instead of the class.

This change first checks whether the package exports the supplied class under its internal name. It scans the other exports only when that name is absent or refers to something else. For ggplot2, it finds `class_ggplot`, so existing subclass definitions work again. The generated constructor still looks up the parent at run time, so upgrading the parent package picks up its current constructor without reinstalling the child package.

The regression test installs small parent and child packages, checks construction, then upgrades only the parent and checks that the child uses the updated constructor.

title: Dispatch on default argument values
description:
S7 currently ignores a generic's default when choosing a method for an omitted argument. Reverse dependency checks found this breaking iAR and ggtime through mixtime:

```r
f := new_generic("x", function(x = NULL, ...) S7_dispatch())
method(f, NULL) <- function(x, ...) "NULL method"

f() # Error: Can't find method for `f(MISSING)`.
f(NULL) # "NULL method"
```

This PR makes `f()` use the default `NULL`, so it returns "NULL method" too. Defaults can also use another argument: mixtime's `chronon_format_linear()` uses `cal = time_calendar(x)` to get the calendar from `x`. Arguments with no available value still dispatch on `class_missing`.

Internally, S7 now checks whether an argument has a value available, including a default. It keeps the original argument expressions so methods can still capture them. Generics without `...` can also supply dispatch defaults; methods leave those defaults to the generic.

The tests and documentation cover these cases.

title: DO NOT MERGE: Reverse dependency results and investigation
description:
**Do not merge.** This draft is only for sharing the reverse dependency results and the investigation into their causes for S7 0.2.2 versus 0.2.2.9000.

The original cloud run checked 121 packages and flagged 48: 37 with new problems and 11 that failed to check. The [investigation](https://github.com/RConsortium/S7/blob/docs/revdep-results/revdep/investigation.md) covers each of those packages, with observed failures, likely causes, proposed repairs, and limits on what was verified.

The main findings concern defaulted dispatch arguments, foreign classes exported under aliases, data-frame validation, legacy saved mappings, and downstream namespace and constructor migrations. The reports include saved reproductions and cited log and source excerpts. A later local run covering 122 packages is included separately because its results include additional environmental failures.

Anansi's original cloud preparation failure remains unexplained because its logs were empty. Parts of the covr, typedjson, and vecvec investigations also remain unresolved. The focused reproductions do not establish that proposed fixes pass full package checks.

All changes are under `revdep/`. No S7 implementation changes or fixes are included.

title: Use exported methods::assignClassDef()
description:
- Swap `:::` with `::` in usage of `methods:::assignClassDef()` to remove the R CMD check note.
- Redocument and update DESCRIPTIONS with roxygen2 8.1.1.

title: Correct evolution vignette examples and deprecation warnings
description:
Clarify that deprecated generics warn when called, while method registration remains silent, matching current S7 behavior.

Also qualify `lifecycle::deprecated()` so the argument-deprecation example works without attaching lifecycle, and update the displayed cross-package constructor to match the generated code.

Documentation only; no runtime changes.

title: Allow deprecated classes to share method registrations
description:
Add `share_methods = TRUE` to `deprecated_class()` so class authors can share methods with a compatible replacement without requiring each downstream method to use an explicit union.

With this option, registering or removing a method for `Old` behaves like registering or removing it for `Old | New`. The default remains `FALSE`. Both classes retain their identities, constructors, and property types.

Sharing applies when methods are registered; it does not copy previously registered methods. Downstream packages that captured the old class definition need to be reinstalled. External class references resolve the definition when the package loads.

Internally, replacement classes expand alongside unions during registration and removal. Package-unload cleanup uses the registered signatures so it can remove shared methods even after the class package unloads. Includes documentation and regression tests.

title: Add optional class aliases to `deprecated_class()`
description:
This is an alternative to [#769](https://github.com/RConsortium/S7/pull/769). That PR keeps two distinct classes and optionally shares method registrations. This PR adds `alias = TRUE` to `deprecated_class()` so the old name uses the replacement's constructor and class identity.

```r
Old := deprecated_class(new = New, when = "2.0.0", alias = TRUE)
```

Calling `Old()` warns and constructs a `New`. Both names resolve to the replacement in method signatures, parents, property types, unions, and inheritance checks. Registering or removing a method through either name affects the same registration. The default remains `alias = FALSE`.

Aliases require `new` and use its definition, so class arguments cannot also be supplied through `...`. Existing objects and subclasses retain their original identity, and previously registered methods are not transferred. Packages that captured the old class definition need rebuilding against the alias.

Internally, aliases to classes in other packages resolve the current exported definition at run time, avoiding serialized copies. Package-unload cleanup uses registered signatures so it also works after the class package unloads. Includes documentation and regressions for class contexts, saved objects, and installed-package upgrades.

title: Strip foreign attributes during S7 construction
description:
`new_object()` now strips foreign attributes when constructing classes rooted in `S7_object`, including properties left over from sibling classes.

`new_S3_class()` gains an optional `attributes` argument declaring the complete set of attributes used by an S3 class. S7 subclasses preserve those attributes when present, along with their declared properties, and discard the rest. The attributes are not required. `NULL` preserves the existing behavior; `character()` declares no attributes beyond class metadata. The bundled concrete S3 wrappers now declare their attributes.

Internally, construction shares the base-ancestor lookup with S4 handling and respects the storage names of S7 properties. Includes documentation and regression coverage for inherited properties, external parents, and bundled S3 classes.

Addresses the attribute leakage described in #760.

title: Resolve foreign parent constructors at run time
description:
When a package defines a subclass of an S7 class from another package, the subclass now calls the installed parent constructor at run time. Parent arguments are forwarded through `...`, so updated defaults and custom constructors take effect without rebuilding the subclass. Inherited property definitions are still captured when the subclass is defined.

Internally, constructor generation reuses the existing external-class forwarding path, including for abstract parents. Subclasses of parents with default constructors keep named parent arguments when both classes are in the same package or the subclass is defined outside a package. Regression tests cover changed parent definitions, and the documentation and NEWS explain that subclassing no longer requires `new_external_class()`.

Fixes #763.

title: Evolution vignette and compat lab
description:
Closes #143.

Adds `vignette("evolution")` for authors changing S7 generics and classes that downstream packages extend. It explains install-time, load-time, and runtime coupling, compatible changes, and deprecation recipes. The packages vignette links to this guidance and explains what external class references resolve at runtime and what remains stored in installed subclasses.

The deprecation guidance covers generic aliases, moves, and retirement; class recommendations that preserve the original identity; and property renames and retirement. It describes when downstream packages need rebuilding and which changes require explicit argument adaptation or saved-object migration.

Adds a manual compatibility lab with 64 scenarios that install real package pairs and compare baseline, upstream-only upgrade, and downstream rebuild behavior, with committed results and a deprecation design review. A release-checklist item prompts maintainers to rerun the lab and update the guidance when behavior changes. This PR changes documentation and developer tooling; it does not change S7 dispatch or construction behavior.

title: Rename deprecated_class() replacement argument to new
description:
Rename the `replacement` argument of `deprecated_class()` to `new` so it matches `deprecated_generic()` and `deprecated_property()`. Class construction, dispatch, and warning recommendations retain their existing behavior.

Update validation messages, regression tests, installed-package fixtures, reference documentation, and NEWS to use `new`. Remove the class deprecation section from the classes and objects vignette.

Local validation: all 1,817 test assertions passed using an isolated installation, and `pkgdown::check_pkgdown()` found no problems.

title: Fix namespace introspection of re-exported bindings
description:
`S7_classes(asNamespace("ggplot2"))` errors when ggplot2 re-exports an imported binding such as `rlang::quo_name` without defining it in the namespace itself. The same lookup affects `S7_generics()`.

Resolve namespace exports with `getExportedValue()` in the shared introspection helper so both functions can inspect namespaces containing re-exports. Ordinary environment lookup continues to use `mget(..., inherits = FALSE)`. Add a public API regression covering locally defined and re-exported S7 classes and generics, alongside a re-exported ordinary function.

title: Fix tibble conversion of S7_methods() results
description:
`S7_methods()` results can now be converted to tibbles, allowing data-frame printers that use `tibble::as_tibble()` to display them without a scalar-column error.

The signature list now explicitly inherits from `list` so vctrs recognizes it as a vector. Regression coverage checks that conversion preserves results for generics with zero, one, and multiple methods.

title: Update S7 1.0.0 release notes
description:
Prepare the S7 1.0.0 release notes with separate sections for breaking changes, new features, performance, and bug fixes. Group entries by topic and clarify the wording, including that the lists accepted by `new_object()`, `set_props()`, and `convert()` are named lists passed as a single unnamed argument through `...` (#497).

Only `NEWS.md` changes. Earlier release notes are preserved; there are no changes to package behavior or internals.

title: Redocument with roxygen2 8.1.0
description: Redocument the package with roxygen2 8.1.0 and use `@export` for the `@<-` S3 method to remove the missing-export warning.

title: Silently ignore missing arguments in constructor
description: As discussed in https://github.com/RConsortium/S7/pull/445, this PR allows missing arguments in a constructor to "skip" setting the property and avoid invoking a custom setter.

title: Polish S4-backed S7 edge cases
description:
## Summary

I am far from an S4 expert, and this branch is heavily LLM-assisted. It addresses correctness issues flagged by automated/agent-assisted code review of the original branch for #659.

One failure mode of that review process is that it can pull in extra complexity: fixes for edge cases that are technically defensible, but may not be worth supporting in practice. Without an explicit decision in the code or tests about what S7 should and should not support, those fixes can look like scope creep. I am too far removed from the S4 ecosystem to make those judgment calls confidently.

@lawremi, could you look over this branch, especially the tests, and help decide which cases matter and which ones we should drop?

The branch currently contains changes for cases where:
- S4 data-part classes lose attributes or `.S3Class` metadata when used as S7 parents.
- S7 subclasses of S4 classes lose property metadata during construction, validation, conversion, or upcasting.
- S4 slot definitions, including renamed slots and package-qualified slot classes, are not checked against the corresponding S7 properties.
- S4 unions and virtual classes are not matched or initialized with the expected package-qualified class identity.
- S4 parent classes with implicit data parts or conflicting slot accessors are accepted.
- S3/S4 method registration misses dispatch markers for S4-backed S7 classes.
- Installed S4 classes expose stale registration metadata when reused by S7 classes.

It also adjusts S4 registration and validation helpers around metadata refresh and validity proxy reuse, and adds regression tests for construction, inheritance, conversion, validation, data-part handling, method registration, and installed-package compatibility.

One thing worth noting is that even though there are already a lot of changes on this branch that build on top of the already large #659, automated code review is still flagging issues and has not yet come back clean. It might be better to split #659 (and some portions of this PR we deem are worth keeping) into a series of smaller, more incremental stacked PRs. That would make each step easier to reason about and review, both for humans and agents.

title: generalize method() to support S3 and S4 generics
description: Seems reasonable for `method()` to work on the same generics as `method<-()`. Still need to add some tests, so marking draft for now.

title: Make S7 generics and methods traceable
description:
Fixes #584.

Allow `trace()` and `untrace()` to work with S7 generics and methods, including tracing both during multiple dispatch. For example, `trace("my_class", browser, where = my_generic@methods)` sets a breakpoint in the method for `my_class`. Traced functions retain their S7 properties and representation metadata, so method lookup, property access, and printing continue to work. `untrace()` restores the original function.

Internally, this declares the S7 generic and method properties as S4 slots, exposes the `.Data` slot needed by R's tracing initializer, and recognizes traced generics during native dispatch and method lookup. It moves `methods` from Suggests to Imports so registration can happen directly during package loading.

R versions before 4.7 use a compatibility initializer that preserves S7 metadata. On R 4.7 and later, S7 uses R's initializer, incorporating the upstream fixes discussed in [r-devel/r-svn#262](https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/262). Those fixes complement the slot declarations and dispatch changes here.

Local measurements on macOS with R 4.6.1, comparing this PR with `main` (`245aaf46`):

- Untraced single and multiple dispatch stayed at about 1.8 µs and 2.6 µs, respectively, before and after the change (1.0× faster, within measurement noise), with no measured allocation.
- Loading S7 increased from about 11 ms to 45 ms with `methods` already loaded (main loads 4.3× faster). This adds about 35 ms once per fresh session for the S4 registrations.
- With an empty tracer attached, single dispatch increased from 1.8 µs to 3.1 µs for a traced method or 3.4 µs for a traced generic (untraced dispatch is 1.7× or 1.9× faster). These costs apply only while tracing is active.

The dispatch and tracing measurements can be reproduced with `bench/method-trace.R` against separately installed builds.

title: Add deprecated_generic(), deprecated_class(), and deprecated_property()
description:
Fixes #727. Fixes #730. Fixes #754.

This PR adds a standard way to deprecate the pieces of an S7 API — generics, classes, and properties — so that old code keeps working but warns users to update.

## API

All three helpers require `when` (the package version when the deprecation began) and share a `method` argument controlling how the deprecation is signalled: `"base"` (the default, a `.Deprecated()`-style warning attributed to the user's call), `"lifecycle(warn)"`, or `"lifecycle(stop)"`. The lifecycle options require lifecycle as a dependency of the deprecating package.

### `deprecated_generic()`

```r
# renamed
summarise := deprecated_generic(new = summarize, when = "1.1.0")

# retired with no replacement
shout := new_generic("x")
shout := deprecated_generic(old = shout, when = "2.0.0")
```

Calling the old name warns then delegates to the target (via call rewriting, so arguments pass through lazily and unmodified). `method<-`, `method()`, `method_explain()`, `S7_methods()`, and deferred external-generic registrations all silently unwrap to the target, so downstream packages keep installing and working. This also mitigates #729 for renames: a stale downstream registration finds the deprecated object and resolves through it.

### `deprecated_class()`

```r
Dog := deprecated_class(new = Pet, when = "2.0.0")
```

Calling the constructor warns then constructs an instance of `new`. In every other context (`as_class()` is the chokepoint: method signatures, `parent`, property classes, unions, `convert()`, `S7_inherits()`, `new_external_class()` resolution) the alias is silently treated as the replacement. The no-replacement form mirrors the generic: `Cat := deprecated_class(old = Cat, when = "3.0.0")`.

### `deprecated_property()`

```r
Basket := new_class(
  properties = list(
    size = class_double,
    deprecated_property("count", new = "size", when = "1.5.0")
  )
)
```

Generalizes the getter/setter pattern from `vignette("classes-objects")` (which now uses it): reading or writing the old name warns and delegates to the replacement, and the generated `default` means the constructor only warns when the deprecated argument is actually supplied. With no `new`, the property stores data itself and warns on access (construction can't warn in that case, since S7 can't distinguish a user-supplied value from the default).

Default `print()` and `str()` omit properties created by `deprecated_property()` without calling their getters, preventing deprecation warnings or errors during printing (#754). Direct access still signals the configured deprecation. Internally, an `S7_deprecated_property` class marker identifies the properties to omit.

## `new_external_class()` now resolves aliases (#727)

`resolve_external_class_req()` no longer requires the exported object's `@name`/`@package` to match the reference, so a class renamed with a plain alias (`Foo <- Bar`) or a `deprecated_class()` keeps working for downstream packages.

title: Record S7 object representation versions
description:
Record representation versions on newly created S7 objects and class definitions so future backward compatibility shims can distinguish stored formats. Instances carry `_S7_version`, while classes returned by `new_class()` carry `S7_version`. Both currently start at `1L`, independently of the package version; older objects remain unversioned and supported.

Initialize the instance marker in the base prototype, standard and custom constructors, and S4 prototypes. Preserve it through serialization and `S7_data<-()`, and strip it when extracting base data or converting to base and S3 classes. Preserve user-supplied `S7_version` attributes on instances.

Internally, share S7 attribute names across conversion and data access, and reuse cached native version integers, attribute symbols, and class strings. Add public API regression coverage and document the format semantics.

Fixes #711.

title: Lazily restore serialized S7 classes
description:
This reduces the serialized size of package S7 objects by storing the class's package and name instead of its definition. On first class access after `readRDS()` or `unserialize()`, S7 resolves the current namespace binding, updates the object's dispatch classes, and validates it once. If validation fails, the reference stays unresolved so a later access can retry (#742).

Internally, each object stores its own external pointer, so restored objects are validated independently. Classes with `package = NULL` retain their definition in a shared environment in the pointer's protected field, allowing them to be restored in a fresh R session. Existing closure and environment class references remain readable. There are no new public functions or arguments.

The constructor benchmark adds serialized-size comparisons for package and local classes.

title: Allow S3 wrappers to declare compact property defaults
description:
Generated S7 constructors embed S3 constructor closures in implicit property defaults. Roxygen reads and deparses those formals, so a `class_data.frame` property puts the constructor implementation in the Rd usage section. This PR fixes the generated expression by letting S3 class definitions supply a compact quoted default.

- Before (body abbreviated): `survey = (structure(function(.data = list(), row.names = NULL) { ... }, class = "S7_constructor"))()`.
- After: `survey = data.frame()`.

`new_S3_class()` gains an optional `default = NULL` argument accepting a quoted call or symbol. The six concrete bundled S3 wrappers provide compact defaults such as `factor()`, `.Date(numeric())`, and `.POSIXct(numeric(), tz = "")`. Base calls use normal lexical lookup in the generated constructor; caller-local bindings do not redirect them. `stats::formula(NULL)` remains qualified so stats need not be attached or imported by the package defining the class. The bundled constructors remain unchanged. The new argument is documented, with NEWS entries for the API and improved signatures.

Internally, `class_construct_expr()` returns a supplied S3 default directly and otherwise follows the existing constructor path. Defaults belong to the class definition, so custom same-name wrappers without a default retain their own closures and captured environments; no class-name lookup is involved. Defaults are evaluated for each object construction, and an explicit `new_property()` default takes precedence. Union selection, inheritance, missing defaults, abstract POSIXt, internal matrix/array wrappers, and S7/external-class references retain their behavior. Arbitrary custom-closure prettification remains out of scope. No runtime dependency is added.

The revised signature regressions failed before implementation. The focused tests passed on R 4.6.1 (463 assertions), as did the full suite (1,459 assertions, no failures, warnings, or skips). The focused tests also passed on R 4.2.3 (459 assertions; one expected R-version skip). `devtools::check(document = FALSE)` on a clean source copy completed with no errors or warnings and two existing notes concerning `methods:::assignClassDef` and `Rf_findVarInFrame`; it used `--no-manual --as-cran`. Documentation was regenerated. `pkgdown::check_pkgdown()` found no problems, and `air format .` and `git diff --check` passed.

A minimal temporary package was processed with roxygen2 8.1.0 on R 4.6.1 using an isolated installation of patched S7. Its generated usage was `Survey(survey = data.frame())`, with no constructor body, and `tools::parse_Rd()` succeeded. The package installed and constructed the default during `.onLoad()` with S7 and stats unattached, including caller-local and global shadow checks. This verification stays outside the permanent suite and adds no roxygen2 dependency. Hosted CI is pending for the updated head.

Closes #755.

title: Cache construction metadata
description:
Prototype for #723.

Classes cache construction metadata in their shared class reference:

- property names with setters
- property storage names
- parent property names
- stored properties requiring validation
- expected base types
- whether a class layer adds any validation work

`new_object()` uses the cache to avoid rediscovering setters and storage names, and skips validation when a concrete parent is already valid and the child adds neither properties nor a validator. `validate_properties()` uses the cached validation plan and reads ordinary non-S4 properties through the native storage accessor used by `prop()`, preserving the handling of properties set to `NULL`. These internal changes improve constructor performance through the existing public APIs.

## Benchmarks

I ran `bench/constructor.R` in three paired runs against main at `6004091a` and this prototype at `39a3ad16`, using arm64 with R 4.6.1. Each run used a fresh process and an archived source tree, with the version order reversed for the second pair. The table gives the median of the three run medians.

| Case               |   Main | Prototype |               Change |
| ------------------ | -----: | --------: | -------------------: |
| Depth 1            |  26 µs |     20 µs |          1.3x faster |
| Depth 5            | 130 µs |    100 µs |          1.2x faster |
| Depth 10           | 270 µs |    220 µs |          1.2x faster |
| One-shot depth 5   |  36 µs |     39 µs |          1.1x slower |
| Width 0            |  25 µs |     20 µs |          1.3x faster |
| Width 2            |  37 µs |     33 µs |          1.1x faster |
| Width 10           |  76 µs |     49 µs |          1.6x faster |
| Width 50           | 280 µs |    130 µs |          2.2x faster |
| Setter             |  38 µs |     35 µs |          1.1x faster |
| Custom constructor |  32 µs |     31 µs | Within session noise |
| Validate depth 5   |  32 µs |     35 µs | Within session noise |

The one-shot constructor's slowdown is near the roughly 10% session drift threshold. Class lookup and inheritance checks showed no clear change.

Marginal class-graph memory was 1.09–1.17x main across the measured depths and widths, using the second result from `lobstr::obj_sizes()` on two equivalent classes. Per-instance memory remained 168 bytes at depths 1, 5, 10, and 20.

title: Implement `S7_user_frame()`, `S7_generic_call()`, and `S7_generic_fun()`
description:
Adds three helpers for use inside methods of S7 generics, including functions called by those methods:

- `S7_generic_call()` returns the nearest call to the generic, with optional argument matching via `match = TRUE`.
- `S7_user_frame()` returns the frame from which the generic was called, for non-standard evaluation.
- `S7_generic_fun()` returns the generic function itself.

`S7_generic_call()` and `S7_user_frame()` default to `skip = "none"`, which keeps the nearest generic call and its caller's frame. Use `skip = "super"` to skip same-generic `super()` redispatches. The helpers aren't supported in methods for S3/S4 generics or operators.

Internally, `S7_dispatch()` records `super()` redispatches in its own frame so the helpers can identify them without adding bindings to the generic's frame. Includes documentation, examples, and tests.

Fixes #596

title: fix unary Ops methods: `-`, `+`, `!`
description:
Fixes #531 by supporting S7 methods for unary `+`, `-`, and `!`, including inheritance, `super()`, and S3/S4 bridging. For `+` and `-`, use a signature of `list(Foo, class_missing)`; `!` takes a single class. Unary calls fall back to base behavior when no method is found.

Internally, operator dispatch returns a private marker on lookup misses instead of throwing and catching errors. Missing-method errors raised inside a selected method now propagate correctly. Operator generics also have fixed argument lists; development-time checks reject extra method arguments, including `...`.

### Benchmarks

Local results from `bench/method-ops.R`, comparing the exception-based implementation (`29ab5796`, which already supports unary operators) with the current implementation (`d6e88b5c`):

| Operation                | Exception-based | Current | Improvement |
| ------------------------ | --------------: | ------: | ----------: |
| Unary `+` fallback       |           26 µs |  2.7 µs | 9.5x faster |
| Unary `-` fallback       |           26 µs |  2.9 µs | 9.1x faster |
| `!` fallback             |           18 µs |  2.7 µs | 6.4x faster |
| Registered unary method  |          5.0 µs |  2.4 µs | 2.1x faster |
| Registered binary method |          6.2 µs |  3.7 µs | 1.7x faster |
| Registered `!` method    |          4.8 µs |  2.4 µs | 2.0x faster |

R 4.6.1 on macOS arm64; medians of three fresh R sessions per installed build, with balanced run order and 10,000 iterations per case. Timed outputs matched across builds. Ordinary generic dispatch changed from 1.7 µs to 1.8 µs, within the 10% noise threshold.

title: Fix shared class references in constructors and S4 registration
description:
Fix two regressions introduced by shared class references in #743. Constructor properties and local variables named `.S7_class_ref` no longer interfere with construction. S7 objects registered with S4 now pass S4 validity checks when they store a shared class reference.

Internally, class-reference lookup is limited to the constructor's enclosing environment, and the private `_S7_class` slot uses `ANY` to accommodate both storage representations. Both single-binding environments also use `hash = FALSE`. No new exported API.

Validation: all 1,315 test assertions pass, including regression tests for constructor name collisions and S4 registration before and after construction, inheritance, and conversion.

title: Keep S7's := ahead of rlang and data.table
description:
Fixes #697.

S7, rlang, and data.table all export `:=`. Before this change, the version found on the search path depended on the order in which the packages were attached, and R could print a masking message.

This PR makes S7's `:=` win in either order. R no longer prints an attach-time message saying that one package's `:=` masks another's. Messages about other masked objects are still shown.

When rlang or data.table is already attached, S7 changes only the `:=` binding that the package added to the search path. It does not change the package namespace, so explicit access with `` rlang::`:=` `` or `` data.table::`:=` `` is unchanged. The original search-path binding is restored if S7 is detached.

The package vignette also shows how to import `:=` from S7 when a package imports rlang or data.table.

## Testing

- The full test suite passes.
- The pkgdown check passes.
- R CMD check completes with no errors or warnings; the two existing notes remain.
- Both attachment orders were tested on R 4.2.3 and R 4.3.3.

title: Fix test fixture namespace cleanup
description:
`local_install_and_attach()` calls `detach(paste0(...))` without `character.only = TRUE`. The resulting error is silently swallowed, leaving fixture packages loaded after their temporary library is deleted. This causes the missing `t2.rdb` error in the [R-devel CI job](https://github.com/RConsortium/S7/actions/runs/36161780625/job/108159828499?pr=756).

Use deferred `unloadNamespace(package)` to detach and unload each fixture before removing its library. This also handles fixtures explicitly unloaded during a test and lets unexpected cleanup errors surface. The change is limited to the test helper; there are no user-facing changes.

title: Reduce copies of S7 class objects
description:
Fixes #742.

This prototype stores an environment-backed class reference on ordinary S7 instances instead of the class closure itself. This avoids the deep copy from `sys.function()` and ensures `saveRDS()` saves a single copy of the object.

The tests use a small internal C `obj_addr()` helper to assert reference identity directly.

title: Restore compatibility with release ggplot2
description:
Fixes #747.

Restores compatibility between development S7 and released ggplot2, fixing failures when loading ggplot2 and constructing plots.

Adds CI jobs that test both source and binary builds of the current ggplot2 release against development S7. Both jobs exercise plot construction and rendering.

Internally, this restores recognition of abstract S3 classes saved by older S7 versions.

It also relaxes S3 property checks: the declared class no longer has to appear at the end of the object's class vector. For example, a property declared as `new_S3_class("Coord")` now accepts an object with class `c("CoordCartesian", "Coord", "ggproto", "gg")`. Declarations containing multiple classes still require those classes to appear together and in order.

`S7_inherits(x, Class)` now also works when an object has the expected class names in its `class` attribute but lacks the stored S7 class definition.

title: Data.frame validation works properly with data.frame and matrix columns
description:
This closes #751 

In addition to data.frame columns that were talked about in the issue, matrix columns were tested here too. `lengths(self)` would have caused the same issue for those type of columns:

```r
mat <- data.frame(y = 1:3)
mat$m <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 3)
mat
#  y m.1 m.2
# 1 1   1   4
# 2 2   2   5
# 3 3   3   6

mat  |> lengths()
# y m 
# 3 6 
```

title: Correctly compute range for factors with missing values
description: Closes #741

title: Increase to testthat version that first introduced skip_unless_r()
description:
This test uses `skip_unless_r()` which was introduced on testthat `v.3.3` (see [release notes](https://github.com/r-lib/testthat/releases/tag/v3.3.0))

```r
test_that("inherits() works with S7_S3_class", {
  skip_unless_r("> 4.3.0")

  expect_true(inherits(factor("a"), class_factor))
  expect_false(inherits(1, class_factor))
  expect_true(inherits(Sys.Date(), new_S3_class("Date")))
})
```

title: Misc S4 fixes
description: Place to compile S4 fixes not directly related to the S4 inheritance work. Will request review when there's reasonable confidence that there won't be another fix shortly forthcoming.

title: Only check method/generic consistency in development contexts
description:
Fixes #726. Fixes #728.

`check_method()`'s consistency diagnostics are only actionable by the developer of one of the packages involved, so this PR only performs them in development contexts, detected by the new `in_dev()` helper. Outside these contexts — e.g. end user loading an installed downstream package whose upstream has changed a generic — `check_method()` skips its checks entirely, so the user doesn't see no errors or warnings they can't do anything about (#728). This moves failures from load time, to run time, thus making more `R CMD check` fixes possible.

Additionally, at `load_all()` time, we demote the incompatibility errors (exact-formals match for `...`-less generics, dispatch-argument mismatch, dispatch-argument defaults) to warnings, so you can still source the package, think fix the problem en masse (#726). 

Tests simulate the contexts with new descriptive helpers (`local_load_all()`, `local_R_CMD_check()`, `local_end_user()`), making the existing snapshot tests deterministic regardless of how the test suite itself is run.

title: Only validate base properties once
description:
Part of #723. Rebased onto current `main`.

For a property restricted to a base type, `prop_validate()` called `class_inherits()` to check the underlying type and then called the base class validator, which checked exactly the same thing again. This is a reasonable hot path since we expect that many properties will be base classes.

## Benchmarks

I benchmarked current `main` (`91f41404`) and this PR locally back-to-back using `bench/constructor.R`, with all comparable expressions in a single randomized `bench::mark()` call.

| Case | Before | After | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 base-type properties | 40 µs | 34 µs | 1.2x faster |
| 10 base-type properties | 100 µs | 70 µs | 1.4x faster |
| 50 base-type properties | 400 µs | 250 µs | 1.6x faster |

Hierarchy construction, zero-property construction, and standalone validation were within the ~10% between-session drift threshold.

title: Cache each class's hierarchy of validators
description:
Part of #723. Rebased onto current `main`. The `@` → `attr()` reads of `validator` and `parent` this originally carried have been dropped — those now belong to #735. What remains are reads of the *new* `S7_validators` cache attribute, which has no `@` equivalent.

Of the four sibling PRs this is the one with the most design in it, and worth the closest review. It's the big win for deep hierarchies.

## What

Validating an object walked up the class hierarchy calling `class_validate()` at every level, paying for `is_S4_class()` and a `class_type()` switch each time, even though almost no hierarchy has any validators at all.

Each class now caches, in a new `S7_validators` attribute, every validator that must run for one of its instances — ordered from the class itself up to the root, named with the owning class's description. It's built incrementally from the parent's cache, so maintaining it costs nothing.

The cache is `NULL`, meaning "walk the hierarchy", when:

* the ancestry contains an S4 or external class, whose validators can only be resolved at validation time; or
* the class was built by an older version of S7 (no attribute).

It's only consulted when `parent` is `NULL`, i.e. when the whole hierarchy is being validated. That's deliberate: the cache describes the *full* ancestry, not the truncated walk that `validate_from(parent = )` performs, so `recursive = FALSE`, the S4-ancestor path, and constructors with an already-validated parent all still walk.

## Numbers

I benchmarked current `main` (`91f41404`) and this PR locally back-to-back using `bench/constructor.R`, with all comparable expressions in a single randomized `bench::mark()` call.

| Case | Before | After | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `validate()` on a depth-five object | 31 µs | 21 µs | 1.5x faster |
| One-shot depth-five construction | 32 µs | 20 µs | 1.6x faster |

Generated constructor chains, wide classes, and the other benchmark cases were within the ~10% between-session drift threshold. This is expected: the cache is used when validating the full hierarchy, while generated constructors validate incrementally against an already-validated parent.

## Why this caches closures, not classes

My first version cached the *class objects* that own validators. It worked and sped up the deep cases, but it **regressed** `wide10` (113 → 120 µs) and `wide50` (418 → 438 µs).

The reason is that `R_sysfunction()` returns `duplicate(cptr->callfun)` (`src/main/context.c:518`, with R Core's own `/***** do we need to DUP? */` comment), and `duplicate()` deep-copies attributes. Since S7 keeps class metadata in closure attributes, every construction deep-copies the class and its whole ancestor chain — so adding an attribute that referenced ancestors made that copy O(depth²).

Caching the validator closures instead removed the regression, because duplicating a closure is cheap: formals, body and environment are shared, and a bare validator has no attributes. (The underlying duplication is addressed separately in draft #740.)

## Also in this PR

If a validator returns something other than `NULL` or a character vector, the error now names the class that owns it. On `main` you get the useless `<S7_class> validator must return NULL or a character, not <double>.`; now it's `<Foo> validator must ...`. Same text from both the cached and walked paths. No existing snapshot depended on the old message.

## Correctness

The cache reads the parent's cache at `new_class()` time, so a class object mutated after creation (e.g. `attr(Foo, "validator") <- ...`) would go stale — already unsupported, and the old walk had the same exposure through `@parent`.

I did *not* try to cheapen the `identical()` in the fallback walk. Comparing `S7_class_name` first would be faster but changes behaviour when two classes in one chain share a fully-qualified name.

New tests cover: every ancestor's validator running for a subclass defined *after* its ancestors (including a base-type root); the invalid-return message from both the cached and the walked path; and an *external* parent's validator still running, which guards the `NULL`-cache fallback. Verified `R CMD INSTALL` works — the `S7_object` bootstrap at build time, where `class_type()`'s DLL isn't available yet, is guarded by the `is.null(parent)` branch.

`devtools::test()`: `FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 0 | PASS 1271`. Snapshots: additions only, no existing snapshot changed.

## Relationship to the other PRs

#736, #737 and #738 are the siblings; all four are rebased onto `main` and independent. This PR and #738 both add an attribute in `new_class()`'s attribute block, so whichever merges second needs a one-line rebase and to add both names to the `prop_names` synchronisation test. Note #735 documents a constraint on that block: no metadata attribute name may be a prefix of another, since the hot-path reads there omit `exact = TRUE`. `S7_validators` satisfies it — but it is *close* to the existing `validator`, so it's worth keeping in mind that the reverse direction (a new attribute named `validator...` shorter than an existing one) is the hazard.

title: Add constructor benchmarks
description:
Adds a reusable benchmark script for constructor performance and per-instance memory usage.

The script:
- compares hierarchy depth, property width, setters, custom constructors, validation, dispatch, inheritance, and property access in one interleaved `bench::mark()` call
- measures marginal instance memory with `lobstr::obj_sizes()` so shared class graphs are counted only once
- supports selecting benchmark groups, saving results, and comparing back-to-back runs

It also documents the project benchmark methodology in `AGENTS.md` and excludes `bench/` from package builds.

title: Use base `attr()` for internal property access
description:
## Summary

S7 now reads class metadata directly with `attr()` in construction and
validation hot paths, avoiding the S3 dispatch overhead of `@`. In the measured
cases, this makes `new_object()` and `validate()` 25-30% faster.

On R 4.3 and later, S7 also no longer defines its compatibility `@` binding, so
remaining internal `@` expressions resolve to base R's generic. On older R
versions, S7 continues to define and export its compatibility implementation,
preserving qualified access to the exported `@` and existing property access
behavior.

## User-facing changes

- Speeds up `new_object()` and `validate()` without changing their APIs.
- Keeps property access behavior unchanged on supported R versions, including
  the exported compatibility `@` on R 4.2 and earlier.

## Internal changes

- Reads known class metadata attributes directly in performance-sensitive
  construction and validation paths.
- Uses exact attribute lookup for `.should_validate`.
- Keeps the conditional namespace export for older R versions and avoids an S7
  `@` binding on R 4.3 and later.
- Adds regression coverage for `validate()` on bare S7 objects and class
  objects.
- Ignores `.claude/worktrees` so local worktrees are not accidentally tracked.

Related to #723.

title: Stash the class in its constructor's environment
description:
Draft, for #723. This is a **memory** fix, not a speed one. Independent of #736, #737, #738, #739.

## The problem

`new_object()` finds the class under construction with `sys.function(sys.parent())`. R's `R_sysfunction()` returns:

```c
return duplicate(cptr->callfun);  /***** do we need to DUP? */
```

(`src/main/context.c:518` and `:525` — the comment is R Core's.) `duplicate()` on a `CLOSXP` shares formals, body and environment, but deep-copies attributes (`DUPLICATE_ATTRIB` with `deep = TRUE`, `src/main/duplicate.c:91`).

S7 keeps all class metadata in closure attributes, so **every construction deep-copies the class and, recursively through the `parent` attribute, its entire ancestor chain**. Every instance then holds that private copy in its `_S7_class` attribute.

Confirmed at the address level: the generator and two separate instances all had distinct addresses, as did each one's nested `properties` attribute.

## The fix

`new_class()` interposes a fresh environment between the constructor and its enclosure and stashes the finished class there; `new_object()` reads it back by reference, keeping `sys.function()` as a fallback.

Per-instance memory, gc delta over 5000 instances:

| depth | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1,434 B | 50 B | 29x |
| 5 | 5,400 B | 48 B | **113x** |
| 10 | 10,632 B | 48 B | 222x |
| 20 | 21,472 B | 48 B | **447x** |

Now flat in depth, where before it grew ~1 kB per inheritance level. All instances of a class share one class object; there's a regression test for that which fails 3/3 without the fix.

## Not a speedup

0.3% of construction time at depth 1 rising to 5.6% at depth 20 — within noise on the constructor benchmark. I make no speed claim. Construction remains superlinear in depth; `sys.function()` was only ~12% of the cost at depth 40, and the rest is elsewhere in the per-level work (the `attributes(_parent)` rebuild, `validate_from()`, `collect_dots()`).

## Scope of the win: it does not survive serialization

Worth being explicit, because it's easy to over-read the numbers above. R's serializer ref-shares **environments** but **not closures** — 50 references to one closure serialize at 50.0x, 50 references to one environment at 1.0x. So:

* Serialized size per instance is **unchanged** (11,447 B at depth 5, before and after). 100 instances: 1,237,988 B before, 1,278,612 B after — +3%, a fixed ~40 kB per class, not per object.
* A single instance is 1.4x larger serialized (104,727 → 145,351 B), rising to ~1.85x at depth 20.
* **After `readRDS()`, sharing is lost** — each restored instance carries its own class copy again, exactly as before this PR.

So the win is for live, in-session objects. (Restoring a *class* and constructing new instances from it does give sharing; it's restored *instances* that don't.) The fact that saving N S7 objects writes the class N times is a pre-existing problem this PR doesn't change, and probably deserves its own issue.

For package-defined classes there's a related subtlety: `tools:::makeLazyLoadDB` externalizes environments into separate DB entries, so after `R CMD INSTALL` the exported generator and the stashed copy are two SEXPs (`identical()` is `TRUE`; they share the environment). I verified on a real installed test package that **all instances still share one class object** and the memory win holds in full (414 B/object, flat) — but for package classes the property is "all instances share one class" rather than the stronger "the class is the generator".

## Alternative worth considering: memoise instead of stashing eagerly

If the serialization growth or the build-time reference cycle is unwelcome, there's a variant that avoids both: leave the interposed environment **empty** at build time, and have `new_object()` memoise `sys.function()`'s duplicate into it on first construction.

* No class in the environment at build time, so no cycle is written into the lazy-load DB and no RDS growth for freshly built packages.
* Costs one duplication per class per session instead of one per construction — so the memory win is retained almost in full.
* Weakens the guarantee from "instances share the generator" to "instances share one copy", which as noted is already the situation for package-defined classes.

I have **not** implemented this. Say the word if you'd prefer it and I'll swap the PR over.

## Design decisions

* **Name `_S7_class`**, matching the instance attribute. Not a syntactically valid R symbol, so no constructor body — generated or user-written — can refer to it.
* **Interposed for custom constructors too**, not just generated ones. This never writes into a namespace or the user's environment. `<<-` from a custom constructor still resolves (verified with a `local()`-captured counter), because the interposed env is a child of the original.
* `attr(object, "constructor")` deliberately keeps the original environment. `Foo@constructor(1)` therefore errors — but it errors identically on `main`, so no regression.
* An `emptyenv()` guard, so `eval(as.call(list(new_object, ...)), emptyenv())` still gives the documented error rather than "the empty environment has no parent". Costs 0.12 µs.

## Things a reviewer should weigh

1. **Interposing on custom constructors changes `environment(Foo)`** for a user-supplied function. Reads and `<<-` are unaffected, but `environment(Foo)$x <- v` would now shadow rather than mutate the original. Restricting interposition to `is_default_constructor(constructor)` is a one-line retreat, at the cost of the win for custom-constructor classes.
2. **A local `frame` binding was added to `new_object()`**, which is near the #607 ALTREP-materialisation comment. That comment concerns `_parent` specifically and the ALTREP tests pass, but that hazard has bitten before.

## Validation

The nested-helper, `local()` and `lapply()` cases already error on `main`; the fallback reproduces that exactly rather than making them newly work.

* `print`/`str`/`format`/`deparse`/`identical` on classes and instances: no recursion from the cycle. `identical()` compares environments by pointer and `props()` doesn't reach the environment.
* **GC handles the cycle**: 500 throwaway classes plus instances leave 176 B/class resident, versus 180 B/class on `main` (that residual is `setOldClass` S4 registration, present either way). No leak.

title: Cut fixed bookkeeping cost in `new_object()`
description:
Part of #723. Rebased onto current `main`. The `@` → `attr()` metadata reads this originally carried have been dropped — those now belong to #735. What remains are reads of the *new* cache attributes this PR introduces (`S7_setter_props`, `S7_dispatch`), which have no `@` equivalent.

## What

`new_object()` runs on every construction, once per level of inheritance, so its fixed costs are paid over and over.

* **Cache the names of properties with custom setters** in a new `S7_setter_props` attribute, replacing `vlapply(class@properties[names(args)], prop_has_setter)` on every construction (2.54 µs → 0.37 µs). Always a character vector, so a missing attribute unambiguously means "class built by an older S7", and there's a fallback for that case with a test.

* **Fast paths for the two common shapes**: no properties supplied at all, and no supplied property having a custom setter. Both skip the setter split and the setter loop; the former also skips the storage rename.

* **Reuse the class's cached `S7_dispatch` vector** instead of rebuilding it on every construction.

* **A fast path in `check_parent()`** for what generated constructors always produce: an S7 object whose class is exactly the parent class (4.10 µs → 1.3 µs).

* **`collect_dots()` returns early** when `...` is empty (1.07 µs → 0.25 µs).

## Numbers

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| no properties | 37 µs | **27 µs** (1.4x) |
| depth1 | 54 µs | **45 µs** (1.2x) |
| custom constructor | 46 µs | 38 µs |
| depth10 | 785 µs | 668 µs |

## A landmine worth knowing about

`check_parent()` **cannot call `class()`**. Its `class` argument is bound to an S7 class object, which is itself a function, so R's function-position lookup finds the argument and `class(parent)` recurses forever — blowing the C stack *during package load*. This uses `oldClass()`; there's a comment saying so.

## Worth a look during review

The `check_parent()` fast path is the change I'd most want a second pair of eyes on. It forces `_parent` marginally earlier than before, ahead of the "class has no parent" and abstract-parent early returns. It can only ever return early on an *exact* class match, and I confirmed a forged `structure(1, class = c("Base", "S7_object"))` is still rejected (no `_S7_class` attribute), so it doesn't loosen the check.

## Not done, deliberately

`sys.function()` is not worth replacing for speed, but it is worth fixing for **memory**: `R_sysfunction()` returns `duplicate(cptr->callfun)` (`src/main/context.c:518`, complete with R Core's own `/***** do we need to DUP? */`), and `duplicate()` deep-copies attributes. Since S7 stores class metadata as closure attributes, every construction deep-copies the class and its whole ancestor chain — so a depth-5 instance costs ~5400 bytes against ~40 for a plain equivalent. That's the subject of the draft #740, not this PR.

`local_constructing()` is the largest remaining per-level item at 2.1 µs, 1.2 µs of which is `defer()`'s `do.call(on.exit, ..., envir = frame)`. Making it conditional needs a cached "has an abstract ancestor" flag, which isn't sound for external classes resolved at run time, so I left it.

## Correctness

`devtools::test()`: `FAIL 3 | PASS 1240` against `main`'s `FAIL 3 | PASS 1239` — same pre-existing environmental failures (fixture package installs; `R CMD check` reports `checking tests ... OK`). No snapshot changes. The #607 ALTREP test (which byte-compiles `new_object` via `cmpfun`) passes; no local binding of `_parent` was introduced.

Also checked by hand: reserved-name properties still stored as `_names`/`_dim`, inherited setters still run, duplicate names in a spliced list still resolve first-wins, abstract classes still error directly and still work as parents, read-only and dynamic properties fine, and a genuine subclass instance as `_parent` is still accepted.

## Relationship to the other PRs

#736, #737 and #739 are the siblings; all four are rebased onto `main` and independent. This PR and #739 both add an attribute in `new_class()`'s attribute block, so whichever merges second needs a one-line rebase and to add both names to the `prop_names` synchronisation test. Note also that #735 documents a constraint on that block: no metadata attribute name may be a prefix of another, since the hot-path reads there omit `exact = TRUE`. `S7_setter_props` and `S7_dispatch` both satisfy it.

title: Support S7 extension of S4 classes and vice-versa
description:
Fixes #456. 

First iteration on enabling an S7 class to extend an S4 class and vice-versa.

The concrete, fail-fast goal is to enable SummarizedExperiment, a complex, central package in Bioconductor, to be rewritten in S7, based on S4 classes defined lower in the stack, like those from S4Vectors and IRanges, while not breaking compatibility with dependent packages, like SingleCellExperiment, via S4 shims extending the S7 classes. SingleCellExperiment is complex and deeply dependent on SummarizedExperiment, so if it continues working, it is a very good indicator.

What has been achieved outside of these improvements to S7:
* Fixed a bug in the methods package related to upcasting S4 objects derived old classes. Should be part of the next patch release, but it will cause release failures in the checks.
* Modified S4Vectors devel branch to use a `class1()` helper to be explicit when it wants the scalar name of the object's class and to ensure that it is robust to S3-style class vectors. Also improved the `setValidity2()` helper so that validity functions are enclosed in the S4Vectors namespace, enabling S4 class objects to remain identical across lazy loading. This is important since S4 class objects end up in the S7 class object, which is carried by S7 objects, and we want them to pass identity checks across packages.
* Rewrote SummarizedExperiment ([branch](https://github.com/lawremi/SummarizedExperiment/tree/s7-migration)) to use S7 classes, S7 generics and S7 syntax for defining methods on upstream S4 generics. Also defined S4 classes with the original names that derive from their corresponding S7 classes as a compatibility layer. It passes its tests, which were ported to S7 while preserving the original logic. 
* Ensured SingleCellExperiment passes tests _without any modification_.
* The path to Bioconductor adoption of S7 is now wide open.

For S7 classes extending S4 classes, the current approach is to instantiate S7 objects, meaning that the S4 bit is not set. The justification is that there are S4 object invariants that an S7 object cannot satisfy, and vice versa. The big one being the return value of `class()`. Instead we have an S7 shim that does a reasonable job of mimicking an S4 object, including slot access, validity checking, and initialization, but _not_ `class()` compatibility. See the evolving man page insert for more details.

When an S7 class is made to inherit from an S4 class, `S4_register()` is automatically called on the S7 class. This branch extends `S4_register()` to declare the S7 properties and `S7_class` attribute as S4 slots, which is helpful for making the S4 class more self-describing but critical in case the S7 class needs to be later extended by S4.

To extend an S7 class using `setClass()`, the S7 class first needs to be registered via `S4_register()` and `S4_contains()` should be called to obtain a suitable value for the `contains=` argument.  `S4_contains()` is an abstraction that currently just requires the S7 properties to be static, ie not using getters and setters, since S4 code using `slot()` would bypass those.  Any instances of an S7-derived S4 class are proper S4 objects, with the bit set and a scalar class vector.

Besides adding and changing hundreds of lines of logic around S4 classes, significant changes to support this in S7 include:
* Made S7 property storage compatible with S4 `NULL` slot sentinels. Until now, setting an S7 property to `NULL` removed the attribute, and S4 does not like it when its slots disappear from the attributes.
* The inheritance checks in `prop.c` need to be robust to scalar class vectors, using `@.S3Class` instead.
* Added S4 method registration for internal generics when S7 method signatures include classes with S4 ancestry. S4 methods on internal generics take precedence over S3 methods, so when S7 defines a method on an internal generic, it should define an S4 method if any of the classes in the signature are S4-derived classes, since otherwise it might be overridden by an S4 method defined for a parent class. S7 must also support multi-dispatch methods on internal generics where S4 supports it. The `dimnames<-()` generic is an example.
* `@<-.S7_object()` needs to support slots defined on S4 children that are not S7 properties, because S4 classes that extend `S7_object` will dispatch to the method, even when the S4 bit is set.

Resolving the two incompatible `class()` return values, scalar vs. non-scalar, is a larger issue. My proposal is that we export `methods:::.class1()` as `methods::class1()` and encourage all S4 code to use `class1()` to make the expectation of a scalar return value explicit. Practically, we could update the core of Bioconductor to adhere to that policy and thus enable new Bioconductor packages to extend the infrastructure with S7.
